summary: This program converts a Celsius temperature to Fahrenheit by handing the value off to a function that does the math and returns the result. The main method then prints both temperatures in one message.

lines.text: The temperature is stored as a double rather than an int so that any decimal places in the conversion are kept instead of being chopped off.

This single line does three things: it calls the function, passes celsius in as the argument, and captures the value the function returns in a new variable. A function with a return type is only useful if you catch what it gives back.
Joining a double to text with + turns the number into part of the message, which is why 25.0 and 77.0 show up with their decimal points.
The parameter here happens to be named celsius, the same as the variable in main, but that is a coincidence rather than a requirement — the two are separate variables and either could be renamed.

Because celsius is a double, multiplying by 9 first produces a double, so dividing by 5 keeps the fraction. Writing 9/5 * celsius instead would divide two whole numbers, give 1, and quietly return the wrong answer.
